\textbf{Source.} Tadelis (2013), \emph{Game Theory: An Introduction}, Exercise 3.7 ``Public Good Contribution'', p.~58 {[}PDF 77{]}. Reproduced verbatim. Answer in the source: none in the book (the preface, p.~xiii, says about half are solved on Princeton UP's website; not checked).

\begin{quote}
\textbf{Public Good Contribution:} Three players live in a town, and each can choose to contribute to fund a streetlamp. The value of having the streetlamp is 3 for each player, and the value of not having it is 0. The mayor asks each player to contribute either 1 or nothing. If at least two players contribute then the lamp will be erected. If one player or no players contribute then the lamp will not be erected, in which case any person who contributed will not get his money back. Write down the normal form of this game.
\end{quote}
